label: paragraph_title
text: MACAO SHOTS.

label: text
text: WHAMPOACADETS' FRESH OUTRAGE.

label: text
text: SEVERAL PEOPLE WOUNDED.

label: text
text: (From Our Own Correspondent.

label: text
text: Macno, Sept. 21.

label: text
text: Under great provocation, a Portuguese Government armed launch refrained from returning the fire, yesterday afternoon, of Whampoa Cadets whose shots from Chinese territory recocheted into Macao, wounding several people.

label: text
text: How the incident started has yet to be investigated. Shipping in Macao waters had been interfered with. The armed launch went to investigate in Macao inner harbour, across which is the Chinese island of Lappa, the foreshore being known as Wan Tani

label: text
text: A boatload of pigs left Macao because the trader failed to sell—not accepting the price offered. One side of the water (really the mouth of a river) is the Macao inner harbour and the other side is Chinese water. The pig junk was interfered with as was another native boat carrying cocoanuts. The Portuguese launch investigated and was met by a fusillade from the Cadets garrisoning Wan Tsai. Nobody on the naval vessel was hit. Two or three on the water-front on the Macao side were wounded.

label: text
text: It is believed that both junks fell into the hands of the strikers and soldiers at Wan Tsai.

label: paragraph_title
text: A BAD FRIEND.

label: text
text: Robs Hs Fellows

label: text
text: Three young Filipino musicians were the complaints in a case which came for hearing before Mr. R. A. D. Forrest at the Central Magistracy this morning when a fourth named Dometrio Abella appeared in the dock on a charge of larceny.

label: text
text: The evidence showed that all four of them were members of a troupe which had lately carried out a tour in Java with their principal, a lady. It was alleged that during the absence of the complainants from the hotel where they lived the accused went through their luggage and stole 150 pesos. He left the hotel immediately and his whereabouts were not known until the Police were informed and he was found in a boarding house at Yaumati. At the time of his arrest the accused was found to be in possession of a new suit case and to have made arrangements for getting away from the Colony unknown to the others.

label: text
text: The accused attempted to justify his action by stating that the others owed him money, but His Worship was not satisfied with this explanation and imposed sentence of three weeks' hard labour.

WIN CUP.

label: text
text: G.O.C. MAKHS. PRESERVATION

label: text
text:
About 750 officers and men of the 1st Battalion, the East Surrey Regiment, were drawn up on the Murray Parade Ground, this morning and presented an imposing sight.
The occasion was the presentation by Major-General C. O. Luard, C.B., C.M.G. of the Young Soldiers' Cup (a challenge trophy of the National Rifle Association) and medals.

label: text
text: Before the presentation, an inspection of the ranks was made by the General Officer. Commanding, who was accompanied by his A.D.C., Captain Swinton. M.C.

label: paragraph_title
text: BORDER INCIDENT

label: paragraph_title
text: CUTTING OF TELEPHONE

label: paragraph_title
text: CHINESE BOY CAUGHT.

label: text
text: It will be remembered that during the recent attacks by Chinese soldiers on the border the telephone line connecting the Sheung Shui Police Station with the other Stations and the military pickets was found to be cut on several occasions.

label: text
text: A strong force is always maintained at Sheung-Shui, where the A.S.P. (Mr. Gerrard) also has his headquarters, hence the desire of the Chinese soldiers to isolate that Station and so prevent the rushing up of reinforcements.

label: text
text: During last month the military field telephone line was twice cut, and a strict vigilance on the part of the pickets to catch the perpetrators was rewarded by the arrest of a Chinese boy yesterday as he crossed the border to carry out the desired object.

label: text
text: It is clear that the Chinese soldiers are using small boys, who would naturally carry out the work of cutting the telephone lines with less chance of detection. The arrested boy will be brought before the Magistrate in due course.

label: paragraph_title
text: AMOY BETTER.

label: text

EMIGRANTS BY BRITISH
VESSEL

label: paragraph_title
text: RUBBER HOOM PRESENTS

label: text
text: Reports of the anti-foreign boycott having considerably diminished at Amoy have reached Hongkong. There may still be a little agitation by bodies which have little influence at present but there is, generally, no animosity to any foreign nation.

label: text
text: The Indo-China S. N. Co.'s "Suisang" left Amoy a few days ago, arriving here yesterday, en route for Singapore. She had on board upwards of 500 Chinese deck passengers. According to Chinese reports there were very enthusiastic scenes at Amo' when the emigrants sailed. They were, it is said, each given a small present in commemoration of the end of the anti-British crisis. These emigrants are attracted to Singapore, continues the report, by the boom in rubber.

label: text
text: It is noteworthy that no cargo's mentioned in the "Suisang's" report.

label: text
text: CHINESE MERCHANTS' PETITION DRAFTED.

label: text
text: TO-MORROW'S MEETING.

label: text
text: The petition of Chinese merchants with regard to proposed measures for the provision of ready cash in order that an effort may be made to meet obligations for the taking up of goods and the transaction of any business which is possible under present conditions has now been finally prepared and is before the Government.

label: text
text: It is understood that the petition does not specify any particular means by which the desired money might be raised, such as the issue of loan bonds or release of bank notes, but leaves it with the Government, in the event of a decision favourable to such loan, to specify measures along which the money should be raised.

label: text
text: A meeting will take place tomorrow between the Government and representatives of the business community to discuss the matter.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: The Foreign Office has received information that civil war is imminent between Chang Tso-lin and Feng Yu-liang. The cabinet voted unanimously for Japanese neutrality if hostilities break out. It is understood there will be no customs Conference in the event of warfare.—Reuter.

LOCAL OPINION.
General opinion among Chinese military officers and politicians in Hongkong is that should the struggle take place between Mukden and the Christian general, the opportunity will be found for Wu Pei-fu to make a rally. One popular report is that Tuchun Hsiao Yao-nan, one of the Yangtse warlords, is raising several millions and an army of 200,000 in Wu's cause. This campaign ought to have far-reaching effects on the political situation all over China.

Tuan Chi-jui sent Yeh Kung-cho to Tientsin to discuss with General Yang, the policy to be followed in Kiangau (the province in which Shanghai stands). Yeh returned to Peking that night.

On the morning of September 20, Chen Teu-yuan went North from Pukow to meet General Yang. At 5 a.m. on September 20, General Yang left Tientsin for Techow. The train stopped awhile and General Yang inspected the troops at the arsenal. On the afternoon of September 20, General Yang reached Tsinan where Chang Jung-chiang, mother him at the station and entertained him to dinner at the Tuchun's yamen, followed by a trip to the Taiming Lake. At 6 p.m. General Yang left Tsinan, southwards for Pukow and is expected at Klangning on the morning of September 22. General Yang brought with him from Tientsin several hundreds of his body guards to go to Klangsu. text: MANY CHINESE INQUIRIES.

label: text
text: Many Chinese are believed to have inquired along the waterfront as to the s.s. "Honam's" next sailing for Canton. The vessel was not alongside the Steambont Co's wharf this morning and was due to be out from dock this afternoon. It is expected that she will make the trip tomorrow, leaving Hongkong at 8 a.m.

label: text
text: The "China Mail" was courteously informed by one of the Chlu On S.S. Co.'s staff that the "Hydrangea" is unlikely to be despatched to Swatow just yet, even though the strike embargo has been removed and a new government set up. During the last week or so, the "Hydrangea" has been alongside her wharf, after undergoing renewal. However, there is talk of sending this ship to Hoihow and other ports on that route.

label: text
text: Rumours were current on the water-front this morning that the Douglas S.S. Co. were considering the prospect of again sending ships to Swatow. Some say that the s.s. "Haich'sg" may leave on Friday but this has yet to be confirmed.

ADVANCED BY ALLEGED
ROBBER.

label: text
text: BOWRINGTON CANAL INCIDENTS

label: text
text: As his defence against a charge of complicity in a robbery in Bowrington Canal Road, one of three prisoners appearing at the Criminal Sessions this morning said that he had come from up country and not being able to get shelter, food or work as a result of his friends having left for running. He was invited to a man whom he did not know and who said he would find him work.

label: text
text: The man in question, said the prisoner, took him to a house and went inside. He later came out running and prisoner ran too and was caught by police. His reason for having a bangle on him stolen from the house was, he said, that the man in question had given it to him.

label: text
text: The sister bangle to the one found on prisoner was produced in court by the Chinese lady occupant of the shop robbed. This witness's story was very different from that of the prisoner already mentioned. She identified the man and others and said that they obtained admittance on the pretext of buying firewood.

label: text
text: Three prisoners were charged in connection with the robbery this morning. One was alleged to have had a revolver in his possession.

label: text
text: The case against them is still proceeding..
